prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2017 manifesto sets out a programme to rebuild Britain so it works for the many, not the few. It rejects austerity and a rigged economy, committing to public investment, fair work, strong public services and a jobs‑first Brexit.

Economy and tax
- National Transformation Fund: £250bn over 10 years for transport, energy, housing, broadband and science, fairly shared across all regions; universal superfast broadband by 2022 and 5G along major routes.
- Industrial strategy: highest share of high‑skilled jobs in the OECD and 60% zero/renewable energy by 2030; National Investment Bank with regional banks to lend £250bn.
- Fair taxation: no rises in income tax for 95% (those under £80k), no VAT or NICs hikes; top 5% and large corporations pay a bit more; clamp down on avoidance and late payments; protect SMEs, revive co‑ops, and give workers a “right to own.”

Public ownership, energy and environment
- Bring rail, mail, water and energy networks back into public hands as franchises or licenses expire; cap energy bills and create local public suppliers; ban fracking; insulate 4m homes; Clean Air Act; plant 1m trees; tackle plastic waste; strengthen animal welfare.

Brexit
- Accept the result; negotiate a close new relationship prioritising jobs, living standards and rights, retaining the benefits of the Single Market and Customs Union; guarantee EU nationals’ rights; reject “no deal”; no hard Irish border; devolved powers to nations/regions; protect EU‑derived rights and standards.

Education and skills
- National Education Service: cradle‑to‑grave learning free at point of use.
- Early years: expand free childcare (including all two‑year‑olds), boost Sure Start, raise staff pay and qualifications.
- Schools: reverse cuts, smaller classes under 30 for infants, free primary meals, end forced academisation/grammar plans, restore teacher pay body.
- FE/HE: free lifelong FE; scrap tuition fees and restore maintenance grants; strengthen apprenticeships and Unionlearn.

Work, rights and social security
- 20‑point plan: equal rights from day one; ban zero‑hours; sectoral collective bargaining; Living Wage £10 by 2020; end tribunal fees and public‑sector pay cap; four new bank holidays; 20:1 pay ratios on public contracts.
- Pensions triple lock; protect winter fuel and bus passes.
- Overhaul Universal Credit (end six‑week wait and two‑child limit), scrap sanctions and bedroom tax; stronger disability support with assessments replaced by holistic, public processes; raise Carer’s Allowance.

Health and care
- NHS: £30bn extra over the Parliament; end privatisation; restore 18‑week and 4‑hour A&E standards; scrap pay cap and reintroduce bursaries; free hospital parking; ring‑fence mental health, end out‑of‑area placements.
- Social care: build a National Care Service; £8bn this Parliament plus a long‑term funding settlement; real living wage for carers; end 15‑minute visits; increase Carer’s Allowance.

Homes and communities
- Build over 1m new homes, including at least 100k a year for social rent/affordable sale; empower councils; suspend Right to Buy until like‑for‑like replacement; three‑year tenancies with inflation‑capped rent rises; ban letting fees; plan to end rough sleeping.
- 10,000 extra police on neighbourhood beats; 3,000 firefighters; protect the Human Rights Act; restore legal aid routes; review Prevent; 3,000 more prison officers; end new private prisons.

Transport
- Publicly owned rail with fare caps, free Wi‑Fi, safe staffing; empower councils to regulate buses and create municipals; complete HS2 and major electrification; expand cycling and clean transport.

Equality, rights and international
- Gender‑balanced cabinet; defend abortion rights (extend to NI); LGBT‑inclusive RSE and legal reforms; tackle racism and hate crime; embed disability rights.
- Foreign policy led by human rights, law and conflict resolution; recognise Palestine; suspend arms to Saudi pending UN probe; meet NATO 2% and renew Trident; maintain 0.7% aid; crack down on tax havens.

This is a fully costed, fiscally responsible plan (no borrowing for day‑to‑day spending) to unlock Britain’s potential and ensure prosperity and dignity are shared by the many, not the few.
